cases.detail: IEEE 1800-2023 7.10.1 requires q[-2:-2] and a slice of an empty queue to be empty. Verilator 5.052 returns all six elements for the negative singleton slice and crashes for an empty queue sliced as q[0:$]. The shared update case aborts in std::deque::operator[]; the standalone EMPTY_QUEUE reproduction segfaults. Its VlQueue::slice compares signed bounds with size_t and accesses index -1 of an empty deque.

cases.detail: Verilator 5.052 orders the indices of an associative array with a signed bit [127:0] index as unsigned: foreach visits 0, 5, -1 and first returns 0. IEEE 1800-2023 7.8.4 orders an integral index of any width numerically, signed or unsigned by the signedness of the index type, so -1 comes first; Verilator orders the unsigned bit [64:0] and packed structure indices of containers::wide_associative_keys as expected, and xezim 0.11.3 orders neither (wide_associative_keys in its review).

cases.detail: Assigning a container of unbounded queues to one of bounded queues generates C++ that assigns VlQueue<VlQueue<unsigned int>> to VlQueue<VlQueue<unsigned int, 2>>, which does not compile (no matching operator=). IEEE 1800-2023 7.6 makes the element types equivalent, and 7.10.5 keeps each assigned queue to its bound. Celox passes the unchanged case.
